title: George Baquet explains the flute-part variation
summary: At the meeting records were played, Baquet did not recognise himself, and he said the variation came from a flute part transposed for clarinet, not from Picou.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: He was a great drummer also. In them brass bands. Oh, he was a great drummer. We went to that meeting. We went to that meeting. Papa Celestine was there. So they began playing records. Disgusting numbers. They played just certain numbers. And they asked George Bakke. Say, can you tell me who was playing that number? George didn't know his own number. George didn't know his own number. He was playing the clarinet. They played it. He said, you know who was that fella playing that clarinet in there? George said, no. He said, well, that's you playing the clarinet in there. It was the number he played in. Well, George Bakke told me how this come about the high society. Because he's the one coming to the road high society, but he ain't the one. He ain't the one. When you want to hear high society, you want to hear Lorenzo Tio play high society. Lorenzo Tio would play that. And we sat down in the meeting nice and quiet. Just serve drinks and everything. So they brought that question up. So they went on and asked Bikku. Bikku ain't had much to say. So George Bakke got up and told him. He was on the job. That's higher than variation come in high society. He was on the job. And they had a flute, but they didn't have no clarinet part for the clarinet. They had a flute arrangement, but no clarinet part. So they're taking the flute part and transposed the flute part and made a clarinet violin solo. They got that variation. They got that off the flute part. That's where they got that from.

Who got it? Who was that? Was that George Bakke then? Yeah, George Bakke. Was the first one that played that off the flute part. Do you remember who the march was by or was the piece by any composer? Do you remember? Was it published? No, no.

He called the name. I'm going to be honest with you. He called the name to me. The man that had the job and the man that composed the number and all. But I just let it slip by. It's hard to remember everything. I'm keeping a memorandum of it or nothing. I just let it slip on by. But he related that to me in the group.
George Bakke told that before Piku.
That's right. And Piku was set there.

I never heard of Piku. You see, I live around Piku House all my days. I never heard of that until at that one meeting. That was around, way around 49, 48. When I heard Piku said, hero, that's very, he doesn't know. Oh, somebody told me what. Because I heard Piku playing counter before I started. Long before I started. Piku, like my mum, has been in his eighties. Long before I started. And Piku was a man. I was a boy. That's why I'm telling you. And he was around here playing with old man Glenn in them.
